rationale.conceptual: Using B3LYP and MP2 with the 6-31G(d) basis set to optimize geometries and compute dihedral angles and energy differences is a standard, routine computational chemistry workflow. No novel or complex theoretical concepts; just running established methods.
rationale.execution: The pipeline requires building initial geometries, running geometry optimizations for 7-8 molecules at B3LYP and 4 molecules at MP2, and one hydrogenation energy calculation. This involves about 15 individual calculations, but they can be automated with a simple script; I/O is straightforward JSON files. No tricky orchestration or multi-tool integration needed.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running standard DFT and MP2 calculations on small organic molecules to extract butterfly bending angles and hydrogenation heats. The method is textbook-level computational chemistry; the pipeline involves a few straightforward steps with open-source quantum chemistry software. Resource needs are minimal (CPU-only, small molecules, small basis set).

compute_estimate.reasoning: All molecules are small (<30 atoms), basis set is modest 6-31G(d). DFT and MP2 calculations on such systems require minimal CPU time and memory (a few GB peak RAM) and no GPU. No external datasets needed.
